literature.title: Suicide‐Related Medical Claims, Downstream Healthcare Costs, and the Economic Impact of Enhanced Outpatient Services
literature.what_it_means: Early coordinated outpatient mental health care was associated with lower subsequent spending, suggesting potential economic value relevant to Waymark's therapist and care-coordination programs. The population was employer-insured, not Medicaid managed care; generalizability requires an explicit argument.

literature.title: Perceived role of digital health technologies for facilitating diabetes self-management and education among low-income adults with type 2 diabetes: a qualitative needs assessment to inform support for newly diagnosed adults
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative needs assessment identifies digital health preferences for diabetes education in low-income population. Payer not reported. No evidence of impact on reach, care-team action, product behavior, or evaluation methods.

literature.title: Ethical implications of screening for loneliness in primary care when intervention capacity is limited
literature.what_it_means: Paper addresses ethical tensions in social-needs screening relevant to Waymark's screening programs, but is normative analysis, not empirical evidence of what works or how to reach/serve populations.

literature.title: Causal inference with real-world data in health care research: a scoping review protocol and study within a review protocol
literature.what_it_means: Protocol describes a scoping review of causal methods on RWD—Waymark's core evaluation challenge. LLM evaluation step aligns with Waymark's AI safety interests. But this is a methods review, not empirical evidence.

literature.title: Digital and artificial intelligence-assisted medication management for older adults with chronic diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
literature.what_it_means: Addresses digital medication management, but population is older adults (not Waymark's adult/pediatric Medicaid focus), payer unspecified, and negative findings on hard endpoints limit actionability for Waymark's pharmacist program.

literature.title: Costs and Quality of Care: Disparities in Heart Failure Diagnosis and Care
literature.venue: The International journal of angiology : official publication of the International College of Angiology, Inc
literature.what_it_means: Review highlights AI-enabled risk stratification, community-engaged care, and attention to social determinants as promising approaches to equity in heart failure care. Relevant to Waymark's targeting and social-needs work, but the abstract does not establish program effectiveness or provide implementation details.

literature.title: Heterogeneous treatment effect estimation with instrumental variable methods
literature.what_it_means: Methods paper on IV + covariate adjustment for heterogeneous effects. Transfer from the rheumatoid arthritis example to Medicaid social-needs populations is untested. Relevance to Waymark's causal evaluation depends on valid IVs and assumptions about residual unobserved confounding in operational data.

literature.title: Digital Health Interventions in Cardiovascular Prevention: Medication Adherence, Risk Factor Management, and Patient Engagement
literature.what_it_means: Systematic review of CVD-focused mHealth and EHR alerts. Touches text messaging (Compass-like) and AI for nonadherence/refills (pharmacy-relevant). No mention of payer, Medicaid population, or social needs. CVD prevention focus differs from Waymark's broad social-clinical mix.

literature.title: Artificial intelligence hallucinations in large language models for medical education and healthcare: a scoping review of detection, mitigation, and governance
literature.what_it_means: This scoping review identifies retrieval-augmented generation, structured prompts, output verification, and human oversight as commonly discussed approaches to managing hallucination-related risks in medical contexts, rather than establishing their effectiveness.

literature.title: Effectiveness of a Multicomponent Digital Therapeutic Program on Inhaled Medication Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
literature.what_it_means: Addresses adherence and behavioral support relevant to Waymark's pharmacy program. The abstract does not report payer or Medicaid status, so applicability to Medicaid managed care is unclear. Most clinical outcomes did not differ significantly; an exploratory symptom-response analysis favored the intervention and warrants further study.

literature.title: Sex differences in ADHD Diagnosis and Care Patterns Among Children Enrolled in North Carolina Medicaid
literature.what_it_means: Describes care patterns for diagnosed pediatric ADHD in Medicaid. May inform how Waymark reaches or treats female children with ADHD, but the study examines diagnosed cases only, not screening or case-finding strategies.

literature.title: Doubly-robust causal inference for multi-valued treatment regimes with recurrent neural networks
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint, not peer reviewed, on causal inference for personalized multi-valued treatments. Evidence is simulation-only, not from Medicaid patients. Relevant to Signal's questions about whom to reach with which action, but not validated in practice.

literature.title: Evaluating methods to quantify the effect of deprescribing a medication on patient clinical outcomes using a simulation study
literature.what_it_means: Methods paper on causal estimation for deprescribing via simulation. No real data, population, or Medicaid setting. Relevant to Waymark's causal-methods interest but does not change operations, reach, or evaluation now.

literature.title: Boundary-stratified safety evaluation of large language models for clinical decision support: a synthetic benchmark in chronic kidney disease renoprotective therapy
literature.what_it_means: Methods paper testing LLM safety on synthetic CKD cases. Relevant to Anchor's verification role but uses synthetic vignettes, not operational Waymark data or US Medicaid populations.

literature.title: Reimagining Maternal Health Through Technology, Community, and System Partnership: Lessons from the InovCares Care Model
literature.what_it_means: InovCares resembles Waymark's integrated model (technology, social needs, care coordination, payer partnership) but targets pregnant people, not Medicaid managed-care members broadly. Payer type and Medicaid status unreported. No causal claims or comparative evaluation.

literature.title: Examining the Active Ingredients of Consultation: Effects of Discrete Consultation Components on Implementation Outcomes for an Autism Intervention in a Community Mental Health System
literature.venue: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
literature.what_it_means: Study examines consultation/training design to improve clinician fidelity and reach for autism intervention. Population is Medicaid-enrolled but intervention and outcomes (clinician adherence, case penetration) do not map to Waymark's programs (CHW, pharmacy, behavioral_health outreach, care_coordination, social_needs navigation).

literature.title: Advancing Social Connection Through Social Prescribing: A Translational and Implementation Science Perspective
literature.venue: Inquiry : a journal of medical care organization, provision and financing
literature.what_it_means: Narrative review of social prescribing implementation identifies a T2-T3 translational gap—screening without accessible intervention pathways. Addresses social-needs navigation workflow but does not evaluate specific program models or populations.

literature.title: Establishing the Clinical Role of Digital Therapeutics in Major Depressive Disorder Treatment
literature.what_it_means: Consensus statements on digital therapeutics adoption could inform Waymark's therapist-delivered behavioral health program design, but the abstract does not report efficacy data, US Medicaid payer evidence, or implementation outcomes specific to community-based care teams.

literature.title: Implementation of Universal PHQ-A Screening in a Predominantly Latine Pediatric Primary Care Clinic
literature.what_it_means: Pediatric depression screening is tangentially related to Waymark's behavioral-health work, but the abstract does not report Medicaid status, payer, or insurance. Setting is safety-net primary care, not Waymark's capitated managed-care model. Population is 12–18 years; Waymark serves adults and pediatric members but focus is unclear.

literature.title: Current and emerging measures and methods for evaluating medication adherence behaviors
literature.venue: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
literature.what_it_means: Addresses measurement of adherence, central to pharmacy programs. Review offers methods guidance but does not evaluate interventions, predict outcomes, or test population reach. No claims about which methods work or whom to treat.

literature.title: Cross-paradigm audit of large language model judges for clinical text evaluation
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses LLM safety and omission-error evaluation (Waymark's methods interest). German language and clinical text types differ from US English care notes. Findings about bias and error-missing may inform Anchor deployment thresholds.

literature.title: Missed opportunities for universal hepatitis C screening in a predominantly hispanic safety-net popaulation: a retrospective cohort study
literature.what_it_means: Identifies a screening gap in a predominantly Hispanic safety-net population and suggests system-level barriers may contribute. Proposes automation and less reliance on clinician decisions. Could inform care-coordination priorities but does not test an intervention.

literature.title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses Waymark's AI-safety interest: how clinicians use AI outputs and risks of reliance. However, review focuses on diagnostic AI for physicians, not population-health decision support, rising-risk prediction, or SMS navigators. Limited evidence on harm; no Medicaid-specific data.

literature.title: Targeting recovery capital for adolescents through treatment for opioid use disorder: a pilot expansion of the Youth Opioid Recovery Support intervention
literature.what_it_means: Uncontrolled pilot with 11 adolescents and no comparator; 7 completed acceptability and recovery-capital measures. Adherence and opioid use were self-reported. The abstract reports no cost or care-system measures. Applicability to Medicaid adolescents remains uncertain; findings are preliminary and insufficient to establish effectiveness.

literature.title: An intensive primary care program for super-utilizer patients—a mixed-methods study
literature.what_it_means: CHW and care-coordination model matches Waymark programs. Super-utilizer population relevant. But no payer reported, weak comparison (one-encounter controls), and no causal design. Mixed-methods adds qualitative insight on trust and social navigation.

literature.title: “How do you recognize the little wins”: Reframing success in individual placement and support from the perspective of program clients and service providers
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative study of what employment program success means to clients and providers. Does not evaluate a Waymark program, test an intervention, or propose measurement methods Waymark uses. No direct bearing on whom Waymark reaches, what care teams do, or how products behave.

literature.title: Real-world evidence for decisions in diabetes
literature.what_it_means: REDDIE's framework for target trial emulation and causal inference directly matches Waymark's stated methodological interests. However, the review focuses on diabetes registries and regulatory contexts; transfer to Medicaid managed-care program evaluation is not explicit.

literature.title: A statistical framework for evaluating the repeatability and reproducibility of large language models
literature.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM output variability evaluation, relevant to Waymark's AI-safety interest. However, validation uses diagnostic reasoning (USMLE, rare diseases), not SMS navigation, care coordination, or population-health decision-making.

literature.title: Longitudinal Associations of Cigarette Smoking, Smoking Intensity, and Smoking TrajectoriesWith Emergency Room Utilization Among U.S. Adults
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed cohort preprint associates smoking with higher subsequent ER use. It could inform Signal's risk ranking and cessation outreach, but does not test an intervention or establish that cessation lowers ER use.

literature.title: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication
literature.what_it_means: Unreviewed preprint proposing diagnosis prediction methods. Abstract does not report payer, population characteristics, or applicability to Medicaid. Signal product suggests next-best actions; diagnosis prediction could inform recommendations, but transfer is uncertain.

literature.title: Therapy-FIS: A Dataset for Assessing Facilitative Interpersonal Skills in Psychotherapeutic Setting
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed preprint presents a dataset and benchmark for automated therapist skill assessment. It could eventually inform Waymark behavioral health quality measurement and supervision, but uses standardized mock-patient tasks, not real clinical encounters, and does not establish applicability to Medicaid care.

literature.title: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM safety and synthetic-population evaluation, relevant to Signal and Compass. But focuses on survey/recruitment simulation, not care-team operations or member outreach. Limited direct operationalization.

literature.title: Algorithmic design choices as determinants of health equity: a causal simulation study of healthcare resource allocation
literature.what_it_means: This unreviewed preprint uses All of Us adult data to simulate how training objectives, features and thresholds affect allocation equity. Its access-independent benchmark could inform fairness testing for Signal, but applicability to Waymark's Medicaid population needs evaluation.

literature.title: Later life precarity and longitudinal frailty trajectories in older adults
literature.what_it_means: Precarity measurement could inform Waymark's social-needs screening and risk stratification. However, UK older-adult population differs substantially from US Medicaid adults; generalizability to working-age members with SMI/substance use unclear.

literature.title: Full-Service Mobile Food Markets and Dietary Quality in Low-Income Housing Communities
literature.what_it_means: Mobile markets address food access, a social need Waymark screens for. This trial found no significant improvement in diet quality or food security, but sodium intake fell. Costs and ROI were not assessed. Waymark would need evidence on costs, uptake and benefits in its Medicaid population before deciding whether to include the program.

literature.title: Medical Respite Care and Changes in Acute Care Use Among People Experiencing Homelessness: A Matched‐Cohort Evaluation in Edmonton, Canada
literature.venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
literature.what_it_means: Housing-adjacent social intervention in a high-needs population. However, Canadian public healthcare system, homelessness-specific setting, and respite care model differ substantially from Medicaid managed care. Authors explicitly flag causal concerns.

literature.title: Evaluating Covered California's Grocery Support Program: A pragmatic randomized controlled trial of a food insecurity intervention
literature.what_it_means: RCT of food insecurity intervention with claims outcomes is methodologically strong and addresses Waymark's core social-needs population. Covered California is exchange, not Medicaid, but design and population plausibly transfer. Results pending.

literature.title: Hallucinations in generative LLMs for radiology: a comprehensive review
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses LLM safety and hallucination risks relevant to Waymark's AI products (Signal, Compass). However, radiology-specific context limits transfer; applicability depends on whether Waymark's LLM deployment faces similar hallucination pathways in care coordination and SMS navigation.

literature.title: Eliminating Safety Clutter in a Safety-Net Hospital
literature.venue: Joint Commission journal on quality and patient safety
literature.what_it_means: The paper addresses EHR alert governance and safety-clutter reduction, relevant to Waymark's AI-safety work and Anchor verification layer. It studies a safety-net hospital, not community-based Medicaid managed care; Medicaid enrollment is not reported. The abstract does not describe the causal evaluation methods of interest to Waymark.

literature.title: A multi-guideline clinical agent for vascular surgery: architecture, implementation, and benchmark evaluation
literature.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM safety and guideline traceability, relevant to Waymark. Answer omissions were not explicitly evaluated. The vascular surgery setting is distant from Medicaid care coordination, behavioral health, and social needs. Benchmark on 55 vignettes, not real-world impact.

literature.title: Multilevel Strategies to Reduce Prostate Cancer Disparities among Black Men in Underserved Communities in Memphis, TN: A Scoping Review
literature.what_it_means: Scoping review of prostate cancer disparities interventions for Black men in underserved Memphis communities. Eight sources were synthesized narratively; the abstract reports no effect sizes. Direct evidence for Memphis-specific interventions and Black male nurse representation remains limited.

literature.title: Primary Prevention ICD in a Contemporary Underserved Population: Factors Associated With Underutilization and Mortality
literature.what_it_means: Examines ICD referral and care coordination in an underserved population, with potential relevance to Waymark. However, the single-center observational design, lack of Medicaid-specific results, imprecise subgroup estimates, and uncertain overall mortality association limit actionability.

literature.title: When fluency outpaces provenance: source traceability and digital health literacy against AI health misinformation
literature.what_it_means: Conceptual framework on LLM health-information safety aligns with Waymark's AI-safety interest. However, no empirical validation, no Medicaid population, and no operational test in managed-care setting yet.

literature.title: Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming
literature.what_it_means: This paper offers a continuous safety-auditing framework for health LLMs, validated against board-certified clinicians. It could inform evaluation of LLM-based features in Waymark's AI products before deployment and aligns with Waymark's stated interest in LLM safety.

literature.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Development: Building Rigorous, Decision-Ready Evidence
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Waymark's causal-evaluation and LLM-safety interests. However, focuses on pharma RCT/RWD integration and regulatory approval, not on population-health program reach, team workflows, or Medicaid operations.

literature.title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
literature.what_it_means: This preprint studies EHR query interfaces with physicians using a research database, rather than testing Waymark's Medicaid care-team workflows. Relevance to the verification layer (Anchor) is indirect.

literature.title: Causal Record Linkage
literature.what_it_means: Addresses methodological foundations for causal inference on linked data—relevant to Waymark's observational evaluation and multi-source data integration. Preprint status and abstract-only framing of solutions limit immediate applicability.

literature.title: Accuracy Is Not Risk: Why Medical AI Should Not Report Only Its Most Likely Label
literature.what_it_means: Addresses risk model calibration and decision-support safety—directly relevant to Signal (risk ranking) and Anchor (verification). No empirical evidence or real-world validation in Medicaid populations provided.

literature.title: Looking Forward to Constructing Better Causal Comparisons
literature.what_it_means: Methodological advance on observational causal inference using foundation models for prognostic scoring. Directly addresses Waymark's core methodological interest in quasi-experimental designs with observational data, but is not yet peer reviewed and shows no Medicaid-specific application.

literature.title: Where Is a Prediction Model Miscalibrated, and for Whom? Local Audits in Outcome-Learned Pockets
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed preprint presents a method for auditing prediction-model miscalibration, potentially relevant to Waymark's Signal product and AI safety work. Tests use synthetic and public data, with no Medicaid or US primary care demonstration. Transferability depends on whether the method works with Waymark's clinical and social features.

literature.title: Evaluation of clinical prediction models: Decomposing performance uncertainty into model development and validation components
literature.what_it_means: Methods paper on uncertainty decomposition in model validation. Relevant to Signal's rising-risk predictions, but abstract provides no empirical test in Medicaid or managed-care settings, and no case study population details.

literature.title: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed preprint models a composite of documented suicide-related codes retrospectively using hospital EHR features and ML interpretation. It may inform Waymark's behavioral health outreach and Signal, but transfer to Medicaid outpatient care is untested. The evidence provides no prospective validation, causal findings, or operational deployment results.

literature.title: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models
literature.what_it_means: Methods paper on EHR model interpretability. Could improve Signal's next-best-action suggestions or Anchor's verification if Waymark deployed similar deep models on outpatient claims/notes. But MIMIC is ICU-heavy hospital data; transfer to ambulatory Medicaid populations unclear.

literature.title: Causal Inference from Self-controlled Case Series
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint, not peer reviewed, on causal identification with SCCS under sufficient assumptions. SCCS is especially useful for rare outcomes. Its fit with Waymark's rising-risk prediction and care coordination is indirect, though it may inform causal evaluation. The abstract does not report empirical validation.

literature.title: Integrating Financial Coaching into Smoking Cessation Treatment for Low-Income Adults Receiving Food Assistance: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial
literature.venue: Journal of health care for the poor and underserved
literature.what_it_means: RCT shows behavioral health + social needs integration improves outcomes in Medicaid-adjacent population. Modest quit-rate difference (22% vs 9%) and modest sample size. Transfer to Waymark's capitated model and care-team delivery requires evidence of implementation fidelity and cost-effectiveness.

literature.title: Social Determinants of Kidney and Cardiovascular Outcomes
literature.venue: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
literature.what_it_means: The review summarizes associations between social determinants and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes, plus policy actions relevant to Waymark's social-needs work. The abstract does not describe specific targeting rules or care-coordination protocols for Medicaid managed-care teams.

literature.title: Primary Care Physicians’ Perspectives on Clinical Integration and Performance Metrics in a Medically Underserved Area
literature.venue: The Journal of ambulatory care management
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative study (n=10) of primary care physicians in one organization serving an underserved Chicago community. May inform how Medicaid care teams understand performance metrics, but transferability is uncertain. Does not directly test interventions, measure patient outcomes, or validate Waymark products.

literature.title: Social Risk Factors of Pediatric Diabetes Patients in Primary Care: Associations From an Urban Health System
literature.venue: Journal of primary care & community health
literature.what_it_means: This cross-sectional study cannot establish causation or validate prospective outreach targeting. Findings from one health system may not transfer to Waymark's populations. The food insecurity association may inform social-needs assessment, but using it to prioritize outreach would require validation in the intended population.

literature.title: Assessment, Intervention, and Ethical Considerations of Artificial Intelligence for Depression and Suicide Risk: A Scoping Review
literature.what_it_means: This scoping review maps evidence gaps and translational maturity in AI for depression and suicide risk, relevant to Waymark's behavioral health and AI safety interests. The provided abstract does not report specific intervention efficacy estimates or Medicaid-specific findings.

literature.title: Barriers to Implementing Bedside Nursing Screening for Health-Related Social Needs in Surgical Patients: An Explanatory Sequential Mixed Methods Study
literature.what_it_means: Study identifies implementation barriers to social-needs screening in inpatient surgery. Waymark does community-based outreach to ambulatory Medicaid members; surgical inpatient context and workflow differ materially. Qualitative design offers implementation insights but limited generalizability.

literature.title: Health-Related Social Needs, Depression and Anxiety, and Asthma Outcomes in Adults with Utilization-defined Mild Asthma
literature.venue: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
literature.what_it_means: Identifies vulnerable asthma subgroup via comorbid HRSN + depression screening, actionable for care teams. Cross-sectional design limits causal inference. Payer/setting unclear; generalizability to Medicaid managed care not explicit.

literature.title: Pandemic electronic benefit transfer benefit disbursement amounts in relation to food security and food spending among low-income U.S. households with children
literature.what_it_means: Food insecurity is a documented social need in Waymark's population. P-EBT findings could inform benefit-navigation strategies and contextualize food-security outcome expectations, but the study does not evaluate a care-delivery intervention.

literature.title: Quantifying benefit and cost-effectiveness of additional investment in community health workers for people with cardiovascular risks in New York City
literature.what_it_means: Models potential CHW benefits for people with obesity, hypertension, and diabetes in New York City. These projections do not establish Waymark's impact in Medicaid. Applicability depends on population and implementation differences; the abstract does not report observational validation of modeled effects.

literature.title: Food Insecurity, Mental Health, and Healthcare Financial Hardship in a Nationally Representative Sample of Hispanic/Latino Adults in the United States
literature.venue: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
literature.what_it_means: This cross-sectional study identifies associations, not causal or treatment effects. It is not specific to Medicaid or managed care. Its mental health and financial hardship outcomes may be relevant to Waymark, but applicability and measurement feasibility need assessment.

literature.title: The Effect of Opioid Abatement Funds on the Utilization of Medications for Opioid Use Disorder
literature.what_it_means: Study measures state-level policy effects on treatment admission rates, not individual Medicaid member outcomes or care delivery. No data on Medicaid-specific populations, managed-care enrollment, or community-based interventions Waymark delivers.

literature.title: A prospective randomized study of patient-centered AI for clinical visit preparation
literature.what_it_means: This unreviewed preprint tests LLM visit preparation among U.S. adults in the Google Health app. Compass is an AI SMS navigator for member requests. Transfer to Waymark's Medicaid population, including members with social needs and behavioral health complexity, is uncertain; Medicaid-specific results are not reported.

literature.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
literature.what_it_means: Relevant to Compass (AI SMS navigator) safety and equitable advice delivery. Audits smoking-cessation advice across simulated user personas, not actual populations. Differences are not necessarily inappropriate: prescription cessation medication is not recommended for minors. Personas differ on several attributes, so individual effects cannot be isolated. Preprint; needs peer review.

literature.title: Accuracy and impact of an AI safety system for missed specialist referrals in primary care
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Anchor's verification function and AI safety methodology. However, Singapore primary care differs substantially from US Medicaid managed care in payer structure, workflow, and regulatory environment. Transfer requires evidence of applicability to US context.

literature.title: Bridging the gap in maternal care: the role of community-based workers in preventing maternal mortality
literature.what_it_means: Commentary on integrating community-based workers into perinatal care, relevant to Waymark's CHW, behavioral health, and social-needs programs. Potentially applicable to Medicaid care, but the abstract provides no Medicaid-specific findings or empirical outcome estimates. It discusses barriers and partnerships rather than demonstrating effectiveness.

literature.title: Toward Standards for Responsible AI in Health Communication: A Dual Method Pre-Deployment Risk Evaluation Framework and Case Study
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed methods preprint evaluates a health communication chatbot before deployment. Its red-teaming and user-testing framework may help assess PII handling, citation reliability, trust, and usability in tools like Compass, but applicability to Medicaid member-facing tools remains untested. It provides no effectiveness evidence.

literature.title: Participant Perspectives on a Food Is Medicine Intervention for Gestational Diabetes Prevention: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study Full Names of
literature.what_it_means: Food-as-medicine aligns with Waymark's social-needs navigation. But this preprint reports a pilot with n=10, no comparison group, and single-coder qualitative analysis. It suggests culturally tailored foods and simpler education, but does not establish operational impact for Waymark.

literature.title: Leveraging generative AI for human understanding: meta-requirements and design principles for Explanatory AI as an emerging paradigm
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Anchor's physician-facing verification design. Proposes design principles for AI explanations that support human reasoning. No empirical test of whether principles improve safety, accuracy, or clinical outcomes in practice.

literature.title: What are the palliative and end-of-life care needs and preferences of people with cancer from culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) backgrounds?: A systematic review
literature.what_it_means: Relevant to culturally competent care coordination and engagement of diverse Medicaid members, but focused on cancer EOL care rather than Waymark's broader chronic disease population and social needs.

literature.title: “Building the connection route to help”: a qualitative study of opioid use disorder recovery processes for black women age 18–30
literature.venue: Journal of Ethnicity in Substance Abuse
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative findings on trusted relationships could inform behavioral health and care-coordination design for young Black women with OUD. Participants’ insurance status is unclear; applicability to Medicaid members needs assessment.

literature.title: Transforming primary care: funding and governance in the shift from physician-centred models to interprofessional teams – a scoping review
literature.what_it_means: Addresses team-based primary care funding and governance, relevant to Waymark's care coordination model. Only a minority of reforms underwent systematic evaluation, and sustainability remains uncertain. The abstract reports no Medicaid-specific effectiveness or cost findings, so applicability to Waymark needs assessment.

literature.title: Evaluating RAG Configurations for Clinical Information Extraction from EHR Notes: Aged Care Case Study
literature.what_it_means: Paper addresses NLP/LLM extraction from notes, which aligns with Waymark's methods interest. However, Australian aged care is not Medicaid managed care; setting transfer is unclear. No evaluation of downstream clinical utility or decision impact.

literature.title: Digital self-management for chronic disease care: a mini review of service integration, equity, and public health implementation priorities
literature.what_it_means: Narrative review of digital chronic disease support; emphasizes integration, equity, and LLM safety—relevant to COMPASS and SIGNAL design. The abstract does not report Medicaid-specific findings, comparative effectiveness estimates, or measured implementation outcomes.

literature.title: Association Between Consulting Multiple Healthcare Facilities and Medication Burden Among Older Outpatients
literature.what_it_means: Consulting more healthcare facilities was associated with higher medication burden among older outpatients—relevant to Waymark's pharmacy and coordination work. The Japanese hospital setting, cross-sectional design, and lack of an intervention limit direct applicability to US Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: Childhood Food Insecurity and the Development of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Dietary, Metabolic, and Psychosocial Pathways
literature.what_it_means: Review identifies food insecurity screening and interdisciplinary intervention as critical but notes insufficient evidence on screening-tool effectiveness. Applies to Waymark's social-needs navigation and care-coordination teams reaching Medicaid children; transfer depends on whether findings generalize to managed-care pediatric populations.

literature.title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
literature.what_it_means: This non-peer-reviewed arXiv preprint examines bias in multi-agent clinical AI, relevant to Anchor's verification role and Signal's next-best-action suggestions. It uses retrospective simulations with MIMIC-IV cases, not real deployment. Transfer to Waymark's capitated Medicaid care is uncertain.

literature.title: Rubricon: Automated Rubric Generation and Refinement for LLM Evaluation and Training
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM evaluation rigor relevant to Waymark's AI safety interests (omission-error detection, output verification). Methods paper with no operational Medicaid data or clinical implementation.

literature.title: Tabular foundation models are not a shortcut to calibrated clinical risk prediction: a pre-registered simulation against the true risk
literature.what_it_means: Relevant to Signal's risk prediction calibration. Preprint on model performance in controlled settings, not real deployment. No evidence that foundation models solve Waymark's out-of-sample validation problem.

literature.title: Rural Readiness: Domain Generalization with Adversarially Chosen Domains
literature.what_it_means: Non-peer-reviewed arXiv preprint on model generalization across domains. Potentially relevant to Waymark's multi-state deployment and model portability, but it provides no empirical validation on Medicaid populations or clinical outcomes.

literature.title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
literature.what_it_means: An arXiv preprint reports safety and clinical performance gains from RL simulation training for psychiatric intake. Relevant to Waymark's behavioral health and AI safety interests, but not yet peer reviewed; testing used simulated encounters, including psychiatrist role-play, not real Medicaid members or care teams.

literature.title: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems
literature.what_it_means: TRACER resembles Signal's rising-risk prediction task. External discrimination was retained, but detection and false-alert burden varied by disease and health system at screening-relevant specificity. This preprint does not report Medicaid-specific evaluation, so operational use warrants caution.

literature.title: Testimony from Timelines: Evidence-Grounded Significance Testing of Temporal Clinical Hypotheses
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM safety in data analysis, which interests Waymark's methods. However, benchmark is vaccine adverse-event data, not Medicaid claims or care coordination. Transfer to population-health observational work is unclear.

literature.title: From prediction to intervention: Causal artificial intelligence as the missing link in precision therapeutics
literature.what_it_means: Review examines causal forests, TMLE and target-trial emulation, methods relevant to Waymark's observational evaluations. Most applications remain hypothesis-generating or retrospective, and the multiomics focus differs from social-needs navigation and population risk prediction in Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: Considering the trade-offs of environmental, social, and governance risk in digital health
literature.what_it_means: Narrative review proposing ESG framework for digital health. Raises safety/governance concerns (ethics, privacy, data) relevant to Waymark's AI products. No empirical evidence on specific trade-offs or mitigation strategies. Medicaid fit unclear.

literature.title: Often Correct, Not Reliably Correct: A Blinded Audit of GPT-5.2 as Guideline-Decision Support for a Rare Cancer (Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma)
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses LLM safety and omission-error evaluation—Waymark's stated methods interest. Its findings may inform checks for omissions in AI outputs, but applicability to Medicaid social-needs navigation and care coordination remains untested.

literature.title: Global Poverty and Social Policy: The Cognitive Costs of Scarcity and Their Policy Implications
literature.venue: Journal of Education Behavior and Humanities
literature.what_it_means: Cognitive-load theory could inform how Waymark designs care-coordination workflows and SMS navigator interactions for members under poverty stress, but the abstract lacks empirical evidence on specific intervention effectiveness or Medicaid populations.

literature.title: My daughter knows over 21 people that have died from drug overdose or suicide: cross-sector rural provider perspectives on adverse childhood experiences
literature.what_it_means: Qualitative provider perspectives on ACEs and community trauma are contextual but lack intervention efficacy data. Rural Missouri differs from Waymark's current states; transferability to Medicaid operations unclear.

literature.title: Medicaid Work Requirements and Behavioral Health: Risks and Opportunities for Peer Support
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses Medicaid policy and peer support integration relevant to Waymark's CHW and behavioral health programs. However, this is a viewpoint, not empirical evidence. No data on outcomes, implementation, or effectiveness.

literature.title: IPF-RAG: temporal-aware retrieval-augmented generation for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis care
literature.what_it_means: Paper addresses LLM hallucinations and reasoning quality—relevant to Waymark's AI safety interests—but focuses on rare disease (IPF) with very small dataset (58 trajectories). No evidence of Medicaid population or transferability.

literature.title: PVminerLLM: structured extraction of patient voice from patient-generated text using large language models
literature.what_it_means: Addresses NLP of patient text for social and experiential signals—relevant to Waymark's COMPASS, Signal and care-note analysis. The model was tested across multiple datasets, but validation in Medicaid settings and impact from integration into care remain unclear.

literature.title: Effectiveness of integrating patient-reported outcome measures into electronic health records for measurement-based care in patients with chronic illnesses: a systematic review
literature.what_it_means: Review examines EHR-integrated PROMs for chronic disease monitoring and care coordination. Waymark uses Signal for risk prediction and care prioritization. Transfer is uncertain: abstract does not report Medicaid populations, insurance type, or social-needs navigation; settings differ from Waymark's community-based model.

literature.title: Examining the Association Between Food Insecurity and Pregnancy Outcomes
literature.what_it_means: Food insecurity was associated with adverse pregnancy and postpartum outcomes among WIC-eligible mothers, a Medicaid-relevant population. The cross-sectional design cannot establish causation. WIC participation did not significantly modify these associations; the study does not establish whether addressing food insecurity would improve outcomes.

literature.title: Compliance by Design: Governing AI ‐Augmented Quantitative Analysis in Clinical and Translational Research
literature.what_it_means: This position paper proposes safeguards for LLM-assisted quantitative analysis, relevant to Waymark’s analytical governance and causal evaluation workflows. Its failure modes—context drift, displacement, and implementation drift—may also inform Anchor’s verification approach.

literature.title: Association Between the Expiration of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program Emergency Allotments and Child Maltreatment
literature.what_it_means: Expiration of pandemic-expanded SNAP benefits was associated with increases in substantiated child maltreatment rates.

literature.title: AI-Enabled Patient Profiling for Personalized Nursing Care and Health Support: Scoping Review
literature.what_it_means: Scoping review of AI profiling methods and applications in nursing. Addresses patient segmentation and personalization relevant to Signal and Compass. However, weak Medicaid fit: no explicit focus on managed-care populations, social needs, or uninsured/underinsured contexts. Most studies evaluate algorithm performance, not real-world clinical impact or safety.

literature.title: Reporting Gaps and Challenges in Randomized Trials of Generative AI for Medical Use: Insights From a Systematic Review
literature.what_it_means: Relevant to Waymark's LLM-safety and omission-error evaluation interests. Identifies reporting gaps in GenAI trials that could inform Anchor validation frameworks. The abstract provides no Medicaid-specific findings or US managed-care operational evidence.

literature.title: Primary Care Engagement Among Adults Hospitalized with Serious Mental Illness
literature.what_it_means: Describes a gap in care engagement relevant to Waymark's target population, but is purely descriptive with no intervention, no causal mechanism, and limited actionability for changing whom to reach or what teams do.

literature.title: Readmission and Treatment Adherence During and After Court-Ordered Treatment in Arizona: A Retrospective Cohort Study
literature.what_it_means: Small retrospective cohort: 29 of 94 identified patients entered paired analyses, limiting power and generalizability. Readmissions were associated with COT expiration; increases in missed appointments and LAI doses were not statistically significant. The SMI population is relevant to Waymark, but Arizona's legal setting limits transfer. Findings may inform transition follow-up.

literature.title: The Program for Education in Drugs and Alcohol for Latine (PEDAL): A Substance Use Spanish-language Curriculum for Community Health Workers
literature.venue: Journal of immigrant and minority health
literature.what_it_means: PEDAL trains CHWs on substance-use recognition and community connection—relevant to Waymark's CHW program. Sample payer and Medicaid status unreported. No outcome data on member-level impacts or care-team workflow changes.

literature.title: Insurance Type and Receipt of Condition-Concordant Behavioral Health Treatment Among U.S. Adults Reporting Past-Year Probation or Parole
literature.venue: The journal of behavioral health services & research
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant population (Medicaid adults with behavioral health needs) and outcome (treatment receipt). However, cross-sectional design, self-report data, and acknowledged inability to infer causality limit actionability. Estimates attenuated after adjustment for coverage gaps.

literature.title: Community Health Worker Interventions Addressing Social Determinants of Health in Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review
literature.what_it_means: This review is relevant to Waymark's CHW work, but does not evaluate its full Medicaid care model. Only 7 RCTs met criteria. Effects on major clinical indicators were modest and inconsistent, while social needs and care engagement showed promise. Evidence of meaningful clinical benefit remains limited.

literature.title: Implementing Culturally Tailored Diabetes Prevention in Hispanic Communities: An Integrative Review Using the RE-AIM Framework
literature.what_it_means: Review identifies CHW models and community-based delivery as implementation facilitators for diabetes prevention. However, abstract does not specify Medicaid population, payer, or managed-care setting; applicability to Waymark's population and programs is unclear.

literature.title: A community health worker pilot intervention to increase patient portal use among people with HIV
literature.what_it_means: CHW support for portal use is relevant to Waymark's CHW model. However, the single-arm pre-post design cannot establish causality. Portal use is an engagement measure; its relevance to Waymark's social-needs, medication, behavioral health and care-coordination work is indirect.

literature.title: Association Between Cumulative Social Determinants of Health and Mortality Among Stroke Survivors
literature.what_it_means: Identifies SDoH indicators associated with mortality among stroke survivors. Relevant to Waymark's social-needs screening and risk stratification, but this observational NHANES study does not test interventions or establish causal mechanisms. Applicability to Medicaid managed care remains uncertain.

literature.title: Toward equitable fidelity measurement of evidence-based psychosocial interventions
literature.what_it_means: Addresses fidelity measurement equity in mental health delivery to underserved populations. Proposes AI automation of fidelity scoring, potentially relevant to Waymark's therapist-delivered services, but is a methods/framework paper without empirical validation.

literature.title: Medication adherence in clinical trials: measurement methods, methodological challenges, and reporting standards
literature.venue: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
literature.what_it_means: Addresses adherence measurement rigor relevant to pharmacist work. However, focuses on trial design and reporting standards rather than real-world Medicaid populations or actionable interventions for care teams.

literature.title: Vaping, Tobacco, and Nicotine Treatment ECHO: A Brief Report on Building Tobacco Treatment Capacity in Missouri
literature.what_it_means: VTN-ECHO trains Medicaid-relevant workforces (CHWs, pharmacists, therapists, social workers) on tobacco treatment. Missouri Medicaid tobacco-use data and mixed-state reach suggest US Medicaid transferability. But no evidence that Waymark members' tobacco outcomes or reach change.

literature.title: Potential savings in Medicaid Antiseizure medication reimbursement, 2008–2025: persistent brand-name reimbursement Despite generic availability
literature.venue: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
literature.what_it_means: Describes reimbursement patterns and generic substitution gaps for a specific drug class. Relevant to Waymark's clinical pharmacy program if seizure management is a population need, but does not evidence an intervention or causal effect on outcomes or reach.

literature.title: Effect of the CP@clinic program (Community Paramedicine at Clinic program) on health care utilization from administrative data during and after the intervention: a cluster-randomized controlled trial
literature.what_it_means: CP@clinic resembles Waymark's CHW/care-coordination model and targets vulnerable populations with social needs. Ontario public insurance and US Medicaid both serve lower-income populations, but eligibility, payment, and provider scope differ substantially.

literature.title: Potential risks of generative artificial intelligence in kidney care
literature.what_it_means: This review discusses GenAI risks in nephrology relevant to Waymark's Signal and Anchor products. It recommends safeguards, structured prompting, validation, and human oversight. The abstract reports no empirical evaluation, Medicaid-specific findings, or detailed validation protocols.

literature.title: The future of medical debt relief in the United States
literature.what_it_means: Medical debt relief is a social need intervention relevant to Waymark members. North Carolina's payment-leverage model is operationally interesting. However, the review highlights gaps in beneficiaries' health and financial outcomes, limiting its guidance on whom to reach or which interventions to prioritize.

literature.title: Unmet social needs in pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease linked to increased risk of missed appointments
literature.what_it_means: In this cross-sectional pediatric IBD study, unmet social needs were associated with more missed medical appointments, but not missed biologic infusions. Causation and intervention effectiveness were not established. Payer was unreported; this specialty gastroenterology population differs from Waymark's broader Medicaid membership.

literature.title: Medication and health-related outcomes by prescription lengths: A systematic review
literature.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
literature.what_it_means: Prescription-length findings may inform Waymark pharmacist workflows and adherence support, but the evidence is heterogeneous and context-dependent. The abstract does not establish applicability to Medicaid members or Waymark's high-risk populations; that would require reviewing the included studies.

literature.title: Trigger-first large language model-assisted adverse drug reaction surveillance: A pharmacist-supervised retrospective cohort study
literature.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
literature.what_it_means: Addresses pharmacist workflow efficiency and LLM safety in ADR surveillance, relevant to Waymark's clinical pharmacy program. However, inpatient hospital setting in China has limited transfer to outpatient Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: Outcomes of a Culturally Adapted Family Model of Diabetes Education and Support for Marshallese Persons With Type 2 Diabetes
literature.venue: The science of diabetes self-management and care
literature.what_it_means: Supports CHW-led DSMES feasibility and an association with improved A1C in a specific cultural community, but no control arm, no Medicaid population stated, narrow geographic/cultural scope, generalizability unclear.

literature.title: Digital health interventions to improve referral documentation: A scoping review
literature.what_it_means: Referral documentation is relevant to Waymark's care coordination and social-needs referrals. The abstract does not specify Medicaid managed-care populations. Applicability depends on whether the reviewed tools fit Waymark's referral workflows and whether findings transfer to its members.

literature.title: Clinician Communication Behaviors and Perceived Health Care Discrimination Among Black Patients
literature.what_it_means: Identifies clinician communication patterns associated with perceived discrimination among Black patients. Relevant to Waymark's diverse Medicaid population and care-team training, but cross-sectional design cannot establish causal impact on adherence, outcomes, or program efficacy.

literature.title: Understanding workplace well-being through appraisal and coping: A qualitative study of promotora/e de salud (community health workers) and leaders’
literature.what_it_means: Addresses CHW workforce wellness and retention—relevant to Waymark's CHW delivery model. Qualitative findings on stress and coping are descriptive, not causal. No intervention tested; no outcome data on performance or retention.

literature.title: Community health worker intervention to prevent incident type 2 diabetes: A cluster randomized trial
literature.what_it_means: CHW intervention in US setting is relevant. However, population is VA/public hospital patients (not Medicaid managed care), prediabetes focus (not Waymark's typical chronic disease/high-need population), and negative primary outcome limit applicability. Increased engagement is noted but not metabolic benefit.

literature.title: Evaluating user experiences with an AI chatbot for health-related social needs: A cross-sectional mixed methods study
literature.what_it_means: Population overlaps Waymark's (Medicaid, unmet social needs). Chatbot design and performance metrics are relevant to Compass. However, cross-sectional design with no control arm cannot measure impact on health, referral uptake, or resource linkage—only user experience. No evidence it changes outcomes.

literature.title: Digital health interventions for patient engagement: A systematic umbrella review
literature.what_it_means: Umbrella review of DHI effectiveness across 42 reviews with diverse populations. Low AMSTAR-2 ratings and exploratory evidence limit actionability. The supplied abstract provides no Medicaid managed-care–specific findings or explicit transfer argument.

literature.title: Design and Impact of Value-Based Payment: A Scoping Review of schemes implemented or active between 2010 and 2024
literature.what_it_means: Scoping review of VBP design and impacts across countries. Waymark operates under capitated Medicaid contracts, but the abstract does not establish coverage of that payment context. Design insights may inform program evaluation frameworks; applicability to Medicaid managed care needs assessment.

literature.title: Electronic Health Record User-driven Evaluations and Adaptations of Large Language Models for Clinical Applications
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Waymark's LLM safety and omission-error evaluation interests. Proposes user-centered framework for clinical LLM alignment and assessment. Narrative review with no empirical results.

literature.title: Informing sample size and power calculations for clone-censor-weight analyses: a Monte Carlo simulation study of the variance inflation factor relative to the underlying target trial
literature.what_it_means: Addresses power planning for observational target-trial emulations, relevant to Waymark's evaluation interests. Provides simulation results and R code to estimate study-specific variance inflation factors for CCW analyses when treatment starts during follow-up.

literature.title: Balancing adaptive delivery and implementation fidelity over time: a longitudinal mixed-methods study of a community health worker–led adolescent nutrition intervention in rural Uganda
literature.what_it_means: CHW supervision and adaptive delivery are relevant to Waymark operations, but the setting (rural Uganda, nutrition, adolescents 10-24) differs substantially from US Medicaid managed care serving high-need adults with chronic disease and mental illness. Transfer requires explicit argument.

literature.title: The Patient Perspectives of Clinical Pharmacist Services in Hospitals and Clinics: A Focused Narrative Review of Qualitative Studies
literature.what_it_means: Patients valued pharmacists' clear communication, medication explanations and availability; some reported role confusion, conflicting information or lack of patient-centredness. These themes could inform Waymark's pharmacy service design, but the review does not establish whom to reach, intervention effectiveness or applicability to Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: Importance of Capturing Risk Adjustment Data for Veterans Using Multiple Healthcare Systems
literature.what_it_means: Potentially relevant to Waymark's multi-source data integration and Signal risk modeling. In Veteran cohorts, adding non-VA data captured more comorbidities and readmissions but changed predictive discrimination little. Whether this finding transfers to Waymark's Medicaid population needs testing.

literature.title: Knowledge-Enhanced Large Language Models for Extracting Clinical Pathway Process Models From Guideline Text: Development and Evaluation Study (Preprint)
literature.what_it_means: Addresses LLM safety and omission-error detection in clinical outputs—core to Anchor product. But evaluation is on guideline extraction, not on care-team decision-making or member outcomes in Medicaid settings.

literature.title: A Knowledge Database of Physical Activity Interventions for Hypertension using Large Language Models
literature.what_it_means: LLM-powered evidence synthesis could support clinical decision-making, but abstract does not address Medicaid populations, social barriers to exercise, or care-team workflows. Preprint with no peer review.

literature.title: Person-centered, trauma-informed care and support for resilience after intimate partner violence: an integrative review through a neurobiological lens
literature.what_it_means: Addresses trauma-informed care principles relevant to Waymark's behavioral health and coordination work with high-need Medicaid members. However, review focuses on IPV-specific populations; generalizability to broader Medicaid cohorts unclear. No US Medicaid-specific evidence presented.

literature.title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Pharmacy: Current Applications, Clinical Evidence, Challenges, and Future Perspectives A Critical Narrative Review
literature.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
literature.what_it_means: Directly relevant to Waymark's clinical pharmacist program and AI safety concerns (Anchor, Signal). However, narrative review synthesizes heterogeneous evidence without primary data. Applicability depends on whether specific AI pharmacy tools discussed transfer to Medicaid managed care.

literature.title: Patient-initiated conversational AI between appointments in breast cancer care: a multidisciplinary clinical and policy perspective
literature.what_it_means: Raises potential safety questions for Waymark's COMPASS: AI-mediated decisions outside care-team view, preference shifts and delayed contact. These are proposed mechanisms, not established patterns. The paper concerns patient-initiated consumer AI in breast cancer care; transferability to Medicaid chronic disease and social-needs navigation is untested.

literature.title: Evaluating the impact of electronic reminders for primary care physicians on lung cancer–screening rates
literature.what_it_means: EHR reminders were associated with higher lung cancer screening uptake. Lower uptake among Medicaid beneficiaries, people farther from screening sites, and active smokers may inform outreach. Waymark's Signal flags rising-risk members; this study does not establish that reminders cause improvement or resolve social barriers.

literature.title: Associations of mental health, substance use and housing instability with hospitalisation outcomes for adults with diabetes complications: a retrospective cohort study in Maryland, USA
literature.what_it_means: Identifies high-risk subgroups (MH+SUD+HI) Waymark targets, but is observational, payer-agnostic, and makes no causal or intervention claims. Authors call for prospective intervention research.

literature.title: CLINES: Clinical LLM-based Information Extraction and Structuring Agent
literature.what_it_means: CLINES aligns with Waymark's interest in care-note NLP and LLM safety evaluation. Its structured outputs could support risk modeling, care coordination and population health measurement, but benefits for Medicaid members were not evaluated. Residual hallucinations require human verification for safety-critical use.

literature.title: Prescription denials for GLP-1 receptor agonists across commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid coverage, 2018-2024
literature.what_it_means: Documents Medicaid pharmacy access barriers relevant to medication review and adherence work, but is observational and does not test an intervention or evaluate Waymark's programs.

literature.title: The Household as Dialysis Infrastructure
literature.what_it_means: Study documents high caregiver burden and social needs (food, transportation, employment) relevant to Medicaid populations. However, small sample, single state, and no intervention or outcome comparison limit actionability for whom to reach or what care teams should do.

literature.title: Association of Adopting Social Determinants of Health Screening Tools in the US Health System with Health, Economic, and Social Needs Outcomes
literature.what_it_means: Scoping review of SDOH screening implementation relevant to Waymark's social-needs program. However, limited evidence on whether screening drives actual need resolution—the critical gap Waymark targets with active navigation and referral follow-up.

literature.title: Emotional and Literacy Adaptation in Large Language Model–Based Medical Guidance: Development and Usability Study
literature.what_it_means: Tests LLM adaptation capabilities relevant to Compass (SMS navigator), but uses controlled benchmark without real patient interaction, outcomes, or Medicaid populations. Findings on emotional recognition gaps could inform safety design.

literature.title: Improving Access to Community-Based Health Services: A Quality Improvement Initiative Addressing Obesity and Depression in a Residency Clinic
literature.what_it_means: Tests referral workflow and provider education—relevant to Waymark's care coordination. However, measures only provider behavior (referrals made), not patient engagement, outcomes, or whom to reach. No comparison group or causal inference.

literature.title: Analysis and Prediction of Relapse Risk Factors in Community-Dwelling Individuals With Schizophrenia: Retrospective Cohort Study
literature.what_it_means: The model could inform whom to reach among people with schizophrenia by identifying hospitalization-related severe relapse risk. Its performance in US Medicaid managed care is not established by this study; use at Waymark would require validation in its population.

literature.title: From Prediction to Interaction: A Behavioral Informatics Framework for AI in Preventive Health
literature.what_it_means: Directly critiques prediction-centric AI design and advocates interaction-centric, behavioral frameworks relevant to Waymark's SMS navigator and risk models. No new data; synthesizes existing evidence into a design philosophy.

literature.title: Moving beyond overconfidence: A clinical roadmap for integrating uncertainty-aware AI models into medical workflows
literature.what_it_means: Directly addresses uncertainty quantification and error detection in AI clinical deployment. Anchor uses AI verification; Signal generates AI predictions. Roadmap for validation and threshold selection is relevant to both.

literature.title: Examining Antidepressant Medication Management Among Medicaid-Enrolled Youth Newly Prescribed Antidepressant Medication
literature.what_it_means: Describes antidepressant adherence gaps and disparities in Medicaid youth—actionable for behavioral health and pharmacy teams. No causal mechanism or intervention tested; identifies targets for improvement but not how to improve them.

literature.title: Service Delivery of Coordinated Specialty Care Programs Participating in the Early Psychosis Intervention Network
literature.what_it_means: Describes CSC program structures and staffing but is descriptive, not causal. Leadership tenure–turnover association is observational. Relevance to Waymark's integrated Medicaid care model and mixed-service teams unclear.

literature.title: Evaluating and Comparing Approaches to Measuring Quality of Postdischarge Mental Health Outpatient Follow-Up Care
literature.what_it_means: Addresses postdischarge care coordination for behavioral health—directly relevant to Waymark's therapist and coordinator teams. However, VA population differs from Medicaid managed care; applicability requires examining whether findings transfer to commercially insured behavioral health discharges or Medicaid populations.

literature.title: Not Just Why, but When and for Whom: Revisiting Common Estimands in Causal Inference
literature.what_it_means: Methodological contribution to causal inference relevant to Waymark's causal-evaluation interests. Preprint on estimand definition and assumptions. No empirical health-services or Medicaid application shown; transfer unclear.

literature.title: CohortFlow: A Steerable Clinical Cohort Curation Agent with Localized Semantic Correction
literature.what_it_means: In a non-peer-reviewed preprint benchmark, localized updates to cohort specifications were associated with lower correction latency and fewer model calls than full regeneration, with similar eligibility-requirement matching accuracy.

literature.title: Cost-based variable selection for prediction models
literature.what_it_means: Potentially relevant to Signal's risk prediction by weighing predictor value against measurement costs and burden. The abstract reports a simulation and three real case studies, but gives limited detail on validation or how harms were valued. Relevance to action ranking or causal evaluation is not established. This is an unreviewed preprint.

literature.title: When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance
literature.what_it_means: Potentially relevant to Signal if its prediction targets are imbalanced and uncertainty scores guide deferral. This unreviewed preprint evaluates synthetic data and neurodegenerative cohorts, not Medicaid social-needs screening. Transferability to Waymark would need validation.

literature.title: Toward a conceptual framework of economic security for health research: a scoping review
literature.what_it_means: Framework clarifies social-needs domains Waymark screens and navigates (housing, food, employment). Could improve targeting and outcome measurement, but does not test intervention efficacy or causal pathways.

literature.title: Primary non-adherence to newly prescribed discharge medications and 30-day adverse outcomes by mental health status: a retrospective cohort study in two tertiary care hospitals in Montréal, Québec, Canada
literature.what_it_means: Unfilled discharge medications may be an adherence target; mental health status was not independently associated with non-adherence. Having any unfilled medication was not associated with readmission; a modest count-based association was exploratory and needs confirmation. Transfer from Québec public drug coverage to US Medicaid needs assessment.

literature.title: Estimating the Health, Economic, and Social Benefits of Obesity Treatment Using Microsimulation Modeling
literature.what_it_means: Models obesity treatment outcomes for 14.9M Medicaid adults with obesity using a synthetic population and published trial, observational and national-data inputs. Could inform whom to reach (Signal) or care pathways (coordination), but needs validation in Waymark's actual population.

literature.title: Prevalence of social risk factors among hospitalized patients with disabilities
literature.what_it_means: Study characterizes social needs among disabled hospitalized patients—relevant to Waymark's social-needs screening. However, limited to acute-care snapshot; unclear if findings transfer to Medicaid managed-care outpatient populations or predict actionable interventions.

literature.title: A Bias-Aware Analytic Framework for Real-World Data with AI-Audited Workflows: Application to Opioid Ordering in Pediatric Oncology
literature.what_it_means: Methods paper on RWD bias detection via LLM auditing; pediatric oncology opioid ordering is distant from Medicaid behavioral health/social needs. Anchor (AI output verification) and Signal (bias in risk models) could benefit from framework principles, but application requires explicit transfer work.

literature.title: Addressing Care Gaps in Chronic Disease Management: A Systematic Review of Nursing Interventions
literature.what_it_means: Case management and telehealth follow-up may inform Waymark care teams, but reported benefits were mixed and few studies directly measured whether care gaps narrowed. The abstract does not report Medicaid-specific findings or targeting algorithms, so applicability to Waymark needs assessment.

literature.title: Development and Pilot Evaluation of a Standardized and Accessible Rubric (OMNI) for Assessing Generative AI in Health Care Contexts: Four-Stage Mixed Methods Study
literature.what_it_means: OMNI’s Completeness and Accuracy domains are relevant to Waymark’s AI-safety interests. Anchor checks outputs for omissions and errors; OMNI could offer a structured rubric for that evaluation. Applicability to purpose-built health AI, agentic systems, and organizational evaluation settings remains untested.

literature.title: Risk of Bias Assessment of Target Trial Emulation (TTE) studies at Regulatory and Policy Decision Points along the Medical Product Lifecycle: Protocol for a Scoping Review and Stakeholder Survey (Preprint)
literature.what_it_means: Current risk-of-bias tools are not specifically tailored to target trial emulation, and their performance remains unclear. This protocol describes a planned scoping review and stakeholder survey to catalog tools and assess their perceived feasibility.

literature.title: In-hospital Medicaid Enrollment Facilitates Follow-up care for Emergency General Surgery Patients
literature.what_it_means: Retrospective cohort showing association between Medicaid enrollment and care access. Could inform Waymark's care-coordination outreach to newly-insured Medicaid members, but single-center design and observational confounding limit generalizability. Causality unestablished.

literature.title: FLAT-WHITE: from target trial emulation to federated high-throughput causal machine learning using decentralized real-world data
literature.what_it_means: FLAT-WHITE directly addresses Waymark's known interest in target-trial emulation and causal inference with observational data. The federated, privacy-preserving design suits Waymark's multi-state operations. However, the application is drug repurposing in Alzheimer's disease—not Waymark's population or care model.

literature.title: Exhaustive adjustment-set selection and causal effects for distribution-valued outcomes, with inference under latent Gaussian spatio-temporal dependence
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint, not peer reviewed, on causal inference under dependence, relevant to Waymark's observational causal methods. The descriptive Medicaid expansion and syphilis surveillance example is illustrative, not evaluative. No program-level claims.

literature.title: Auditing evaluation artifacts and data leakage in large language model systems for rare disease diagnosis
literature.what_it_means: This methods preprint addresses LLM evaluation rigor and data-leakage detection, relevant to Waymark's AI safety interests. It audits rare-disease diagnosis using public and independent clinical cohorts; applicability to US Medicaid managed care and operational care delivery remains unestablished.

literature.title: Prior-Data Fitted Networks for In-Context Off-Policy Evaluation
literature.what_it_means: This unreviewed preprint explores off-policy evaluation without online experiments—relevant to Waymark's causal-methods interest and potential Signal validation. Its semi-synthetic clinical example is proof-of-concept only; evaluation on real Medicaid data or continuous, high-dimensional member or care-team data is not shown.

literature.title: Precedence-Aware Resource Allocation: Extending the AUTOC Framework to Multi-Level Treatments
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint on ranking-based allocation under precedence and budget constraints, relevant to Waymark's causal-evaluation interests. The supplied abstract does not report empirical validation. Could inform Signal's next-best-action logic for multi-step interventions.

literature.title: Shape-Preserving Treatment Effects for Functional Outcomes
literature.what_it_means: Methods preprint, not peer reviewed, on functional outcomes and time-varying effects. Relevant to Waymark's causal-methods interests, but the abstract identifies no Medicaid population or evaluation of Waymark programs. Its real-data application concerns weight trajectories after medication initiation.

literature.title: Beyond Physical Illness: Can Clinical Narratives Reveal Emerging Mental Health Risks in Chronically Ill Patients?
literature.what_it_means: NLP-based risk prediction aligns with Signal's next-best-action logic and Waymark's interest in LLM safety. However, MIMIC-III is acute inpatient (not community-based Medicaid managed care), preprint lacks peer review, and 'preliminary results' suggests incomplete validation.

literature.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
literature.what_it_means: Relevant to Anchor's omission-error detection across care phases. But this cancer-specific specialty benchmark does not establish applicability to Medicaid care. Its methods design, lack of a causal comparison, and preprint status limit immediate applicability.

literature.title: Risk and Protective Factors of Food Insecurity Among Children in Low-Income Families in the United States: Application of the Multiple Disadvantage Model
literature.venue: European journal of investigation in health, psychology and education
literature.what_it_means: Identifies risk and protective factors for child food insecurity that could inform screening and referral priorities. Sample is low-income but payer/Medicaid status not specified. Cross-sectional design limits causal inference.

literature.title: AI-Assisted Clinical Decision Support Versus Standard Teleconsultation in Adult Medicine: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Accuracy, Referral and Testing Decisions, and Clinician Confidence
literature.what_it_means: Anchor checks AI and clinical outputs for omissions and errors. This review finds low or very low certainty evidence on AI-assisted adult teleconsultation. Evidence is insufficient that it reduces unnecessary referrals or meaningfully increases clinician confidence. Applicability to Medicaid is unclear.

literature.title: Effects of Telenursing on Self-Care and Healthcare Outcomes in Patients with Heart Failure: A Systematic Review
literature.what_it_means: Telenursing's remote contact and adherence support overlap with Waymark's care coordination. The abstract does not establish whether findings transfer to Medicaid members or social-needs work, and it does not report the included study designs needed to assess causal strength.

literature.title: Examining Regulatory Classifications and Social Determinants of Health in Telehealth-Mediated ADHD Prescription Fulfillment Barriers
literature.what_it_means: Among adults using telehealth for ADHD, Schedule II controlled stimulant use was associated with substantially more prescription fulfillment difficulty than non-controlled medication use. Difficulty paying medical bills was also associated with access difficulty.

literature.title: The Nuances of Cost-Related Medication Non-Adherence in Patients Receiving Immunosuppression Compared to Patients with Chronic Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study
literature.what_it_means: Identifies a high-risk subgroup (immunosuppressed + chronic disease, ages 30–49) with elevated cost-related non-adherence. Waymark's pharmacist and social-needs teams could target this population, but the study does not test an intervention or mechanism.

literature.title: Unmet Social Needs Moderate the Relationship between Cooking Frequency and Self-Rated Diet Quality
literature.venue: Journal of nutrition education and behavior
literature.what_it_means: Cross-sectional online survey of US adults; the abstract does not specify Medicaid enrollment, payer type, or a care-delivery setting. Associations may inform planning but do not establish whom an intervention would benefit or support causal attribution. No intervention was tested.

literature.title: Verifying Facts in Patient Care Documents Generated by Large Language Models Using Electronic Health Records
literature.what_it_means: VeriFact addresses verification of statements present in documents. The abstract does not report detection of omitted information. Medicaid fit is weak: no payer, insurance, or US Medicaid managed-care setting reported; benchmark is discharge summaries, not care coordination or community health workflows.

literature.title: Medication Adherence in Cardiovascular Patients: A Qualitative Meta-Synthesis of Perceptions and Experiences
literature.what_it_means: Synthesizes perceptions driving non-adherence in a chronic-disease population Waymark serves. Identifies actionable barriers (side effects, cost, complexity, forgetfulness) and facilitators (reminders, family support, trust). Relevant to pharmacist and CHW interventions.

literature.title: Supporting the Supporters: Feasibility and Acceptability of Balint Groups for Burnout Among Psychiatric Caseworkers
literature.what_it_means: Addresses workforce burnout in mental-health-adjacent roles (caseworkers vs. Waymark therapists/coordinators). Transferable population, but no direct Waymark program change; evidence weak (small n, no control, primary outcome null).

literature.title: Association between food insecurity and five cardiometabolic conditions in a national network of federally qualified health centers
